blocks.text:
The cashier scanned the final item and pushed the receipt toward me.
“Your total is $123.47.”
Chicken.
Milk.
Coffee.
Laundry detergent.
Fresh vegetables.
A box of cereal Mark always complained about if we ran out.
Nothing extravagant.
Nothing unusual.

I inserted my card into the reader.
The machine beeped.
DECLINED.
I frowned.
“That can’t be right. Could you try it again?”
The cashier nodded.
Another beep.
DECLINED.
I opened my banking app.
The account balance was still there.
I had money.
The card wasn’t expired.
There was no warning from the bank.
My face began to burn as people waited behind me.
Then my phone rang.
Mark.
I answered immediately.
“Mark, my card just got declined. Did the bank freeze something?”
There was a short silence.
Then he laughed.
“I froze it.”
I stared at the phone.
“You what?”
“You heard me.”
“Why?”
“Because I’m tired of you spending money without asking.”
I glanced at the groceries.
“Mark, these are household groceries.”
“You don’t get to decide that anymore.”
His voice was calm.
Almost rehearsed.
“From now on, you ask me before you spend anything.”
Then I heard a familiar voice in the background.
